lesson_title: Synoptic Charts: Decode the Weather Map
hook_text: This tiny circle of symbols is a full weather report. Let's crack it in 60 seconds.
clip_script: The circle itself reports cloud cover, measured in eighths of the sky — oktas. Ours is six-eighths shaded: three-quarters of the sky is cloudy. To the upper left sits the air temperature: 18 degrees Celsius. Below it, the dew point: 16 degrees. Compare them — only two degrees apart. Air needing to cool just two degrees to saturate is air already nearly full of moisture. The wind comes as a shaft with feathers. The shaft flies into the circle from the direction the wind blows from — north-west. A full feather counts 10 knots; two full feathers: 20 knots. Read it in one breath: mild, very humid, sky three-quarters clouded, fresh north-westerly wind. This station feels like weather is coming.
visual_style: Zoom into a station model on a real-looking chart, each symbol highlighting and translating into plain text labels one by one.
pacing: Rapid symbol-by-symbol decode with a suspenseful final line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and track the cold front across the chart.
